tower-of-hanoi.title: Identify already‑correct disks
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Compare the initial and goal configurations to find disks that are already on their final peg and in the correct relative order; these disks can be left untouched, reducing the problem size.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: At the very start of solving any Tower of Hanoi configuration.
tower-of-hanoi.example: If disk 5 is already on the goal peg and no larger disk exists, treat it as fixed and ignore it in subsequent planning.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Determine descending placement order
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To build the final stack, larger disks must be placed on the goal peg before any smaller disk that should sit above them, because a larger disk cannot be placed on a smaller one.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After identifying which disks still need to be moved.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Move disk 4 before disk 3, then disk 2, then disk 1 onto the goal peg.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear blocking disks before moving a larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the target disk is not the topmost on its peg, first relocate every smaller disk that sits above it to other pegs; only then can the larger disk be moved.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to move a disk that has smaller disks on top of it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: To move disk 4 from peg 0, first move disks 1 and 2 elsewhere.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use auxiliary peg for temporary storage
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When clearing blocking disks, place them on the peg that is neither the source nor the intended destination of the larger disk, ensuring they do not interfere with later moves.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During the clearing step for a blocked larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: While moving disk 4 to peg 2, move disk 1 to peg 1 (the auxiliary peg) and later move it elsewhere when needed.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Avoid premature placement on the goal peg
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Never move a smaller disk onto the goal peg if a larger disk that must end up below it has not yet been placed; doing so would block the larger move.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When deciding where to temporarily store a small disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Do not place disk 1 on the goal peg before moving disk 4 onto it, because disk 4 could not later be placed under disk 1.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Re‑stack displaced smaller disks after larger ones
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Once a larger disk has been moved to its final position on the goal peg, move the previously displaced smaller disks onto the goal peg in descending order, preserving the correct stack.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Immediately after a larger disk has been placed on the goal peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: After placing disk 4, move disk 2 onto the goal peg, then move disk 1 on top of it.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Track top disks and legality of each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Maintain a mental (or written) representation of each peg’s stack, updating it after every move, and before each move verify that the source disk is the topmost and that the destination’s top disk (or empty peg) is larger than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Throughout the entire planning and execution of the move sequence.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Before moving disk 3 from peg 1 to peg 2, check that peg 1’s top is disk 3 and peg 2’s top (disk 4) is larger than 3.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Simulate and verify final configuration
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After constructing the full move list, replay the moves from the initial state to ensure every move is legal and that the resulting configuration exactly matches the goal state.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Just before outputting the final move list.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Run through the 11 moves and confirm peg 2 ends with [5,4,3,2,1] and pegs 0 and 1 are empty.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Placing a larger disk onto a smaller one
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may forget the size rule and focus only on moving the desired disk.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always compare the moving disk’s size with the destination peg’s top disk (or empty) and ensure the destination is larger.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a disk that is not the topmost on its peg
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may overlook the ‘only top disk can move’ constraint when scanning the pegs.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before each move, explicitly check that the chosen disk is the top element of its source peg.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Temporarily placing a small disk on the goal peg before a larger disk that must be below it
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may treat any empty space on the goal peg as safe for temporary storage.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Reserve the goal peg for the next larger disk to be placed; use the auxiliary peg for temporary holding of smaller disks.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Leaving blocking disks on the target peg when moving a larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may move a larger disk without first clearing all smaller disks from that peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before moving a larger disk onto a peg, verify that the peg’s top disk (if any) is larger than the moving disk; if not, relocate the smaller disks first.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Failing to verify that the final configuration matches the goal
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may assume the constructed sequence is correct without a final check.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Replay the entire move list from the initial state and compare the resulting stacks to the goal configuration before answering.
